docs.title: RadarSim
docs.text: RadarSim is a radar simulator I wrote to study how a surveillance or fire-control radar actually behaves: when a target is first detected, why a track is lost in a hard turn, how much a self-screening jammer hides an aircraft, what sea clutter does to a sea-skimming missile. It runs the physics look by look, shows the result the way a radar display would, and lets you change the radar while it runs.

docs.title: What it models
docs.text:
• Detection from the radar equation with pulse compression, Swerling 0–4 targets, non-coherent integration and CFAR loss. A target is looked at only when the beam passes over it, so detections and tracks arrive at the real revisit rate.
  • Propagation: ITU-R P.676 gaseous absorption, ITU-R P.838 rain with a P.839 rain height, and line of sight over procedural or hand-placed terrain on a 4/3 Earth.
  • Clutter: constant-γ land clutter, the Oh–Sarabandi–Ulaby bare-soil model, the NRL sea-clutter model, rain volume clutter, all entering through the elevation beam, plus an MTI canceller with the Skolnik improvement factor.
  • Electronic attack: barrage and spot noise jamming with burn-through, DRFM range and velocity gate pull-off, chaff clouds and decoys released during the run.
  • Tracking: track-while-scan with global nearest-neighbour assignment, χ² gating, two-point initiation and Kalman/EKF filters; monopulse angle measurement.
  • Signal level: a coherent pulse-Doppler chain (LFM matched filter, MTI, windowed Doppler FFT, CA/GO/SO/OS CFAR) and range-Doppler SAR focusing.

Every model states its references and validity range in the code, and the test suite checks each one against closed-form results or published values (Validation).

docs.title: Licence and citation
docs.text: RadarSim is MIT-licensed. If you use it in published work, please cite it using CITATION.cff in the repository.

A rebuild of the simulator around a correct detection loop, a new desktop interface and a cleaned-up package. Scenario files, the Python import path and two sign conventions changed, so this is a major release; see Migrating from 3.x below.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
• The package is now radarsim instead of src: from radarsim.simulation.engine import SimulationEngine.
  • One coordinate frame everywhere: ENU (x East, y North, z Up), azimuth clockwise from North.
  • Doppler is fd = −2·vr/λ with vr positive when opening; closing targets have negative radial velocity in every output.
  • Scenario files are validated against a schema. Unknown keys are errors with a suggestion; required_radar_preset and other unused keys were removed.
  • Removed modules that did not work or were never connected: advanced/ (except SAR/ISAR, now radarsim.signal.sar_isar), sensor fusion UI, LPI waveforms, RF spectrum view, WebGL renderer, the matplotlib 3-D view and the old Sphinx documentation.

docs.title: Detection and physics
docs.text:
• Detection happens only when the beam centre crosses a target (circular, sector and stare scans), giving one look per revisit.
  • Pulse-compression gain and the compressed range cell were missing (up to 26 dB of error); noise, jamming and clutter now combine after the matched filter.
  • Mean RCS in the SNR with the Swerling statistic only in Pd, removing a double-counted fluctuation.
  • Exact Swerling 1 and 2 detection probabilities, Gauss–Legendre integration for cases 3 and 4, cached; checked against a pulse-level Monte Carlo.
  • CFAR loss from the Gandhi–Kassam closed forms for CA, GO, SO and OS.
  • Clutter enters through the elevation pattern; MTI improvement factor per Skolnik with a 50 dB stability limit.
  • Rain attenuation limited to the ITU-R P.839 rain height; P.676 receives the dry-air pressure.
  • Terrain masking with Earth bulge, terrain presets and height_above_terrain_m.
  • Coordinated-turn motion, deploy times for chaff and decoys, chaff bloom and decay.
  • Every random draw goes through one seeded generator; reset() reproduces a run exactly.

docs.title: Tracking
docs.text:
• Track-while-scan inside the engine with continuous white-noise acceleration, two-point initiation with a velocity gate, misses only when the beam looked, revisit guard and maximum coast time.
  • Rewritten monopulse estimator (squinted Gaussian beams).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
• New desktop interface: dark console theme, IBM Plex type, own icon set, PPI, B-scope, A-scope, RHI, range–Doppler and 3-D views.
  • Simulation runs at a fixed step on its own thread; rendering adapts to the machine (16, 33 or 50 ms frames) with motion interpolation and a reduce-motion setting.
  • New: Pd–range coverage diagram, Monte Carlo panel with Wilson intervals, event log with CSV/JSON report export, scenario editor that draws on the scope and saves canonical YAML.
  • English and Turkish.

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
• radarsim --headless SCENARIO --duration --seed --out and radarsim --list; built-in scenarios ship inside the package.
  • MkDocs documentation with figures generated by tools/make_figures.py and screenshots by tools/capture_screenshots.py.
  • CI runs ruff, mypy, bandit, the translation check, tests on three systems, a wheel check outside the repository and a strict docs build; tagged releases build Windows, Linux and macOS applications.

docs.title: Migrating from 3.x
docs.text:
1. Replace src. with radarsim. in imports.
  2. Re-save old scenarios: load the file, fix the keys the validator reports, and check that positions and headings follow ENU with azimuth from North.
  3. If you post-process Doppler or radial velocity, flip the sign of values from 3.x.
  4. python run_gui.py still works from a checkout; radarsim is the installed command.
Patch release resolving scenario execution edge cases, dynamic parameter synchronization, and command-line scenario loading.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Phosphor Persistence Rendering Freeze: Replaced on-the-fly QPainter brush creation with a pre-cached discrete brush palette in PPI Scope and B-Scope, eliminating GUI freezing at startup and speeding up phosphor updates from 117 ms to 0.5 ms.
  • Sub-1GHz Attenuation Safety: Guarded ITU-R P.676 atmospheric absorption and ITU-R P.838 rain attenuation for frequencies below 1.0 GHz, returning 0.0 dB rather than raising an out-of-domain exception. Resolves crashes in stealth_deep_penetration.yaml.
  • Terrain Type Normalization: Added "mountain" alias and normalization in ClutterModel.ground_clutter_sigma0 to match scenario specifications. Resolves crash in mountain_ambush.yaml.
  • Dynamic Radar Parameter Synchronization: Converted SimulationEngine._radar_params to a real-time property synchronized with self.radar, ensuring GUI frequency/power slider changes immediately affect SNR and detection calculations.
  • Windows Console Encoding: Replaced Unicode arrow and lambda characters in console logging to prevent UnicodeEncodeError on CP1252/CP1254 environments.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Scenario-Bundled Distribution: Bundled the scenarios/ directory in release ZIP/TAR.GZ archives so standalone executables have immediate access to all 10 scenario definitions.
  • Built-in Scenarios Menu: Added File > ⚡ Built-in Scenarios menu for instant one-click scenario launching without manual file browsing.
  • Command-Line Scenario Loading: python run_gui.py [scenario_path] and radarsim [scenario_path] now accept a scenario YAML/JSON file path directly on startup.
  • GUI File Filter: Added *.json to QFileDialog scenario open filter alongside *.yaml/*.yml.
  • Public API: Added MainWindow.load_scenario(filepath) for modular and programmatic scenario loading.
  • Automated Scenario Verification: Added regression test executing multi-step simulation on all distributed scenarios.

This release replaces several approximate or placeholder paths with physically traceable implementations. It is a major release because signal-array shapes and calibration, tracking/fusion semantics, imaging behaviour, package metadata, and removed modules can affect existing callers.

docs.title: Physics and detection
docs.text:
• Corrected monostatic link-budget, thermal-noise, atmospheric/rain, polarization, Albersheim, Swerling, and seeded validation behaviour.
  • Added validated Oh 1992 bare-soil and NRL 2012 sea-reflectivity models with documented domains.
  • Added resolution-cell surface area, signal-to-noise-plus-clutter, Weibull/K clutter, and rain-volume calculations.
  • Added aggregate receiver input-power accounting and a circular-complex Gaussian hard-limiter/Bussgang distortion diagnostic.

docs.title: Signal processing
docs.text:
• Rebuilt pulse-Doppler acquisition around delayed complex LFM samples, linear matched filtering, fast/slow-time phase, physical axes, ambiguity metadata, window coherent gain, and equivalent noise bandwidth.
  • Calibrated CA, GO, SO, and OS one-dimensional CFAR thresholds and added true rectangular two-dimensional CA-CFAR.
  • Reworked stripmap SAR raw-data generation and range-Doppler focusing with non-circular fractional RCMC and calibrated coordinates.
  • Reworked ISAR compression, zero-filled profile alignment, and angular-rate cross-range mapping.
  • Omega-k and chirp-scaling entry points now explicitly report that they are unavailable instead of returning another algorithm’s result.

docs.title: Tracking and fusion
docs.text:
• Added NIS/chi-square gating, globally optimal Hungarian assignment, consecutive confirmation, exact coast/delete timing, and simulation timestamps.
  • Replaced explicit covariance inversions with stable solves and Joseph-form updates where applicable.
  • Added latency-aware constant-velocity timestamp alignment and joint multi-estimate covariance intersection.
  • Separated independent-Gaussian information fusion from unknown-correlation covariance intersection.

docs.title: ECM and simulation
docs.text:
• Added validated DRFM configuration, capture/pull/hold timing, RGPO/VGPO bounds, non-wrapping CPI injection, and radar-relative false-target placement.
  • Corrected exact SJNR combination and receiver saturation propagation into detection diagnostics.
  • Extended scenario round trips for receiver full scale, pulse integration, ground-surface parameters, and DRFM controls.

docs.title: Desktop, packaging, and documentation
docs.text:
• Unified the installed radarsim and source run_gui.py entry points on PySide6.
  • Wired target-inspector probability of detection to the simulation’s Swerling calculation and corrected SAR display normalization and metrics.
  • Removed obsolete optional modules and binary assets; RadarSim has no remote-service dependency.
  • Added UI smoke tests, strict lint/test/security/package CI, and tag-driven multi-platform PyInstaller release builds.
  • Replaced legacy phase notes with model equations, limitations, methodology, architecture, user guide, primary references, and release notes.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• 341 automated tests across supported Python versions.
  • Ruff source/test lint, Bandit medium/high-severity scan, package build, Sphinx warnings-as-errors build, and offscreen PySide6 smoke coverage.

• Added initial SAR/ISAR, multi-radar fusion, DRFM/ECCM, EKF, and pulse-Doppler modules.
  • Added PySide6 scientific displays and scenario examples.
  • Several algorithms from this line were revised or removed in 3.0.0; use the 2.4.0 tag for historical behaviour.
• Initial open-source radar equation, target simulation, tracking, ECM, visualization, and export release.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
These hold everywhere in the code, the scenario files and the interface.

Quantity Convention Frame local East-North-Up: x East, y North, z Up, metres Altitude z above the local ground plane; above mean sea level when terrain is loaded Azimuth from North, positive clockwise (towards East); returned in (−180°, 180°] Elevation from the horizontal plane, positive up Heading direction of horizontal motion, same convention as azimuth Radial velocity \(v_r = \dot R\), positive when the target recedes Doppler \(f_d = -2 v_r / \lambda\): closing targets have positive Doppler Angles in code radians; degrees only in fields ending _deg Power watts in linear expressions, dB / dBm in log form; \(10\log_{10}\) for power ratios Time seconds of simulated time; the engine advances in fixed steps dt

The helpers in radarsim.physics.geometry (polar_from_enu, enu_from_polar, azimuth_from_enu, wrap_to_pi) are the only place these conversions are written out; everything else calls them.

The extended Kalman filter keeps its own internal polar angle (atan2(y, x)) and is fed Cartesian positions by the tracker, so its convention never leaks out.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SpaceEngineerSS/RadarSim.git
cd RadarSim
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[gui,dev,docs]"

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
pytest                                   # tests (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen on headless machines)
ruff check .                             # lint
mypy radarsim --exclude radarsim/ui/     # types of the core package
python tools/i18n_check.py tr            # untranslated interface strings
python benchmarks/engine_benchmark.py    # step and frame cost per scenario
mkdocs serve                             # documentation at http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
radarsim/
  physics/      radar equation, propagation, clutter, RCS, ECM, terrain, metrics
  signal/       waveforms, CFAR, pulse-Doppler, antenna patterns, SAR/ISAR
  tracking/     Kalman, EKF, track manager, monopulse
  simulation/   engine, objects, frames, events, analysis, recorder, headless runner,
                multi-radar network
  io/           scenario schema, loader, exporter, replay, reports
  ui/           desktop interface (theme, widgets, views, panels, controller)
  scenarios/    built-in scenarios (package data)
tests/          pytest suite
tools/          figure, screenshot, translation and release helpers
examples/       runnable API examples
benchmarks/     performance scripts

Physics, signal, tracking, simulation and io never import Qt; the interface talks to the engine only through ui/controller.py and receives immutable FrameState snapshots from the simulation thread.

docs.title: Rules I keep
docs.text:
• Every model states its reference and validity range, and comes with a test against something independent of the implementation.
  • No unexplained constants: a number that is not a physical constant has a comment saying where it comes from.
  • Random draws go through the engine's numpy.random.Generator, so a seed reproduces a run.
  • Conventions in Conventions are not negotiable.

docs.title: Adding a translation
docs.text: Interface strings are wrapped in tr("…"). Add radarsim/ui/assets/i18n/<code>.json, run python tools/i18n_check.py <code> --write to fill in the missing keys, translate them and add the language to LANGUAGES in radarsim/ui/i18n.py.

docs.title: Desktop builds
docs.text:
pip install -e ".[gui,build]"
pyinstaller --noconfirm --clean RadarSim.spec    # dist/RadarSim/

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
1. Update version in pyproject.toml and add a section to CHANGELOG.md.
  2. Tag vX.Y.Z and push the tag.
  3. The release workflow runs the full CI, builds the wheel and the Windows, Linux and macOS applications, publishes them with checksums and the changelog section, and deploys this documentation.

docs.title: Desktop builds
docs.text: The release page has ready-to-run builds for Windows, Linux and macOS (RadarSim-<version>-<platform>). Unpack the archive and start RadarSim (RadarSim.exe on Windows, RadarSim.app on macOS). No Python installation is needed.

docs.title: Installing with pip
docs.text:
RadarSim needs Python 3.9 to 3.12.

python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install "radarsim[gui]"
radarsim

Without the gui extra you get the simulation library and the command-line runner, which have no Qt dependency.

From a clone of the repository:

git clone https://github.com/SpaceEngineerSS/RadarSim.git
cd RadarSim
pip install -e ".[gui,dev]"
python -m radarsim

docs.title: First run
docs.text:
The application opens with the basic_tracking scenario: an X-band surveillance radar and three targets about 40 km out. Within a few seconds you should see

  • the sweep line turning clockwise on the PPI,
  • small plots appearing where the beam crosses each target and fading over one revolution,
  • track symbols (T1, T2, …) once a target has been detected on three consecutive scans,
  • entries in the event log at the bottom: first detections, tracks initiated and confirmed.

Click a target on the scope or in the list on the left to see its range, SNR and the outcome of its last look in the inspector. Change any radar parameter on the right and the next look uses it.

Other scenarios are under File › Built-in scenarios. The scenario catalogue explains what each one is for.

docs.title: Without the interface
docs.text:
radarsim --list                                  # built-in scenarios
radarsim --headless f16_vs_sa6 --duration 120    # summary per object
radarsim --headless naval_battlegroup --out looks.csv --seed 4

See Command line and Python for batch runs and the Python API.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
radarsim [scenario] [--headless] [--duration S] [--seed N] [--out FILE] [--list]
  • radarsim opens the desktop application; radarsim f16_vs_sa6 opens it with that scenario (a built-in name or a file path).
  • --list prints the built-in scenarios.
  • --headless runs the scenario without the interface and prints one line per object: looks, detections, empirical Pd, time of first detection and median SNR, followed by the number of tracks.
  • --out looks.csv (or .json) writes every detection opportunity with all loss terms: SNR, Pd, atmospheric and rain loss, clutter loss, jamming loss, receiver headroom and so on.
$ radarsim --headless f16_vs_sa6 --duration 120 --seed 3
F-16 vs SA-6 Air Defense  (120 s simulated in 0.70 s)
object                      looks   det     Pd  first det [s]  median SNR [dB]
F-16 Alpha                     12     0   0.00              -             -9.7
F-16 Bravo                     12    12   1.00            7.4             39.6
Chaff 1                         6     6   1.00           67.7             51.9
ADM-160 MALD                    9     9   1.00           37.7             42.2
tracks: 3 (3 confirmed)

The same seed always gives the same run.

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
Load a scenario and run it:

from radarsim.io.scenario_loader import ScenarioLoader, resolve_scenario

engine = ScenarioLoader(resolve_scenario("naval_battlegroup")).create_simulation_engine()
engine.seed = 7
log = engine.run(60.0)

for result in log.detection_history[:5]:
    print(f"{result.time:6.1f} s  target {result.target_id}  "
          f"SNR {result.snr_db:5.1f} dB  clutter loss {result.surface_clutter_loss_db:4.1f} dB")

for event in engine.event_log:
    print(event.time, event.kind.value, event.message)

Build a scene in code:

import numpy as np
from radarsim.simulation.engine import SimulationEngine
from radarsim.simulation.objects import Radar, Target, MotionModel
from radarsim.physics.rcs import SwerlingModel

radar = Radar("S-band", position=np.array([0, 0, 20.0]), frequency_hz=3e9,
              power_watts=200e3, antenna_gain_db=35, beamwidth_deg=1.5, scan_rate_rpm=12)
target = Target(1, position=np.array([0, 60e3, 4000.0]), velocity=np.array([0, -250.0, 0]),
                rcs_m2=2.0, swerling_model=SwerlingModel.SWERLING_1,
                motion_model=MotionModel.CONSTANT_VELOCITY, affiliation="hostile")
engine = SimulationEngine(radar, [target], dt=0.05, seed=1, enable_clutter=True)
engine.run(30.0)
print([(t.id, t.status.value) for t in engine.tracks])

Coverage and Monte Carlo, using the same per-look physics as a run:

from radarsim.simulation.analysis import probe_engine, coverage_curve, monte_carlo_pd

probe = probe_engine(engine)            # radar and environment, no targets
curve = coverage_curve(probe, rcs_m2=1.0, swerling=1, altitude_m=3000, max_range_m=150e3)
print(curve.range_pd50_m, curve.range_pd90_m)

Batch studies for a single target against a parametric radar are in radarsim.simulation.headless_runner and scenario_generator; see examples/single_target_study.py and examples/monte_carlo_sweep.py, which runs a seeded range × RCS sweep on all cores.

More self-contained snippets are in examples/api_tour.py.

docs.title: The interface
docs.text:
The window has five parts:

  • Header: scenario name, mode (LIVE, PAUSED, REPLAY, EDIT), simulated time and the current display rate.
  • Objects (left): every object in the scene with its range, or masked / jammed. Chaff and decoys appear when they are released.
  • Scopes (centre): six views of the same picture, switched with the tabs or the keys 1–6.
  • Inspector and settings (right): the selected object, then the radar, processing, environment and electronic-attack settings.
  • Drawer and transport (bottom): events, coverage and Monte Carlo tabs above the play/pause, step, restart, speed and record controls.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
PPI: plan position indicator, North up, centred on the radar. Plots (small dots) appear only where the beam has looked and fade over one revisit period. Track symbols are squares: hollow while tentative, filled when confirmed, amber while coasting, with a one-minute velocity leader and a 2σ uncertainty ellipse. Ground truth uses the NATO affiliation shapes and colours (circle friend, diamond hostile, square neutral, quatrefoil unknown; × for chaff and decoys) and can be hidden with T to see only what the radar knows. A noise jammer shows as a red strobe along its bearing.

B-scope: azimuth against range. For sector-scanning radars the horizontal axis is the sector.

RHI: height against ground range along one bearing, with the terrain profile and the elevation beam. It follows the selected object, otherwise the antenna. Heights are drawn relative to the radar's tangent plane, so the Earth curves away below the horizontal.

A-scope: power above noise along the current beam. Noise is a fresh square-law realization each frame. The dashed line is the detection threshold for the configured false-alarm rate plus the CFAR loss; a noise jammer in the beam raises the floor by its jammer-to-noise ratio.

Range–Doppler: the output of the coherent pulse-Doppler processor (matched filter, MTI, Hamming-windowed Doppler FFT). It is off by default because it is the most expensive part of a step; switch it on from the view or in the settings. Dashed lines mark the blind speeds.

3D: an OpenGL view of the scene and the terrain. It loads the first time you open it; on machines without OpenGL it shows a note and the rest of the program is not affected.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Every field writes straight to the running simulation, and the panel is read back from the simulation when a scenario loads, so what you see is what is simulated. Hover a label for a short explanation. Values use the units shown in the field (GHz, kW, µs …).

docs.title: Analysis drawer
docs.text:
• Events: first detections, tracks initiated, confirmed and lost, terrain masking, jamming and burn-through, with a filter. File › Export report writes these together with a per-object summary (looks, detections, first detection range, median SNR) as CSV or JSON.
  • Coverage: single-look Pd and SNR against range for a probe target, computed with exactly the physics of the current run. The 50 % and 90 % detection ranges are printed next to the plot.
  • Monte Carlo: repeats independent looks at a set of ranges and plots the empirical Pd with 95 % Wilson intervals against the theoretical curve.

docs.title: Scenario editor
docs.text: Tools › Scenario editor (Ctrl+Shift+E) pauses the run and rewinds it to the start. Place object puts a new aircraft where you click on the PPI, heading for the radar; the inspector then edits its name, affiliation, RCS, fluctuation model, altitude, speed, heading and turn rate. File › Save scenario as writes the result in the normal scenario format. File › New scenario starts from an empty scene.

docs.title: Recording and replay
docs.text: The record button (Ctrl+R) writes the session to an HDF5 file in the application data folder. File › Open recording plays it back with a time slider; the speed buttons work in replay as well.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: The simulation advances in fixed steps on its own thread, independent of how fast the screen is redrawn. The display aims for 60 frames per second, extrapolates motion between simulation frames, draws only the visible scope, and drops to 30 or 20 frames per second by itself when frames take too long. View › Performance › Light fixes 30 frames per second and turns off antialiasing and the sweep afterglow for older machines. View › Reduce motion turns off interface animations.

docs.title: Keyboard
docs.text: Key Action Space play / pause . single step while paused R restart the scenario 1 … 6 PPI, B-scope, RHI, A-scope, range–Doppler, 3D + / − or mouse wheel range scale F fit all objects T ground truth on/off Esc clear selection Ctrl+O / Ctrl+S open / save scenario Ctrl+E export report Ctrl+R record Ctrl+J show or hide the drawer F11 full screen

docs.title: Language
docs.text: View › Language switches between English and Turkish; the change applies after a restart.

docs.title: References
docs.text: The source behind each model. Equation and section numbers in the code refer to these editions.

docs.title: Radar fundamentals and detection
docs.text:
1. M. I. Skolnik (ed.), Radar Handbook, 3rd ed., McGraw-Hill, 2008. ISBN 978-0-07-148547-0.
  2. M. A. Richards, Fundamentals of Radar Signal Processing, McGraw-Hill, 2005. ISBN 978-0-07-144474-3.
  3. D. K. Barton, Radar System Analysis and Modeling, Artech House, 2005. ISBN 978-1-58053-681-3.
  4. F. E. Nathanson, Radar Design Principles, 2nd ed., SciTech, 1999. ISBN 978-1-891121-09-8.
  5. B. R. Mahafza, Radar Systems Analysis and Design Using MATLAB, 3rd ed., CRC Press, 2013.
  6. J. V. DiFranco and W. L. Rubin, Radar Detection, Prentice-Hall, 1968.
  7. P. Swerling, "Probability of Detection for Fluctuating Targets," IRE Trans. Information Theory, 6(2), 269–308, 1960. doi:10.1109/TIT.1960.1057561
  8. W. J. Albersheim, "A Closed-Form Approximation to Robertson's Detection Characteristics," Proc. IEEE, 69(7), 839, 1981. doi:10.1109/PROC.1981.12025
  9. P. P. Gandhi and S. A. Kassam, "Analysis of CFAR Processors in Nonhomogeneous Background," IEEE Trans. AES, 24(4), 427–445, 1988. doi:10.1109/7.7185
  10. H. Rohling, "Radar CFAR Thresholding in Clutter and Multiple Target Situations," IEEE Trans. AES, 19(4), 608–621, 1983. doi:10.1109/TAES.1983.309350
  11. E. B. Wilson, "Probable Inference, the Law of Succession, and Statistical Inference," J. American Statistical Association, 22(158), 209–212, 1927.

docs.title: Propagation and scattering
docs.text:
1. ITU-R P.676-13, Attenuation by atmospheric gases and related effects, 2022.
  2. ITU-R P.838-3, Specific attenuation model for rain for use in prediction methods, 2005.
  3. ITU-R P.839-4, Rain height model for prediction methods, 2013.
  4. J. S. Marshall and W. McK. Palmer, "The Distribution of Raindrops with Size," J. Meteorology, 5(4), 165–166, 1948.
  5. Y. Oh, K. Sarabandi and F. T. Ulaby, "An Empirical Model and an Inversion Technique for Radar Scattering from Bare Soil Surfaces," IEEE Trans. Geoscience and Remote Sensing, 30(2), 370–381, 1992. doi:10.1109/36.134086
  6. V. Gregers-Hansen and R. Mital, An Improved Empirical Model for Radar Sea Clutter Reflectivity, NRL/MR/5310--12-9346, Naval Research Laboratory, 2012.

docs.text:
1. D. C. Schleher, Electronic Warfare in the Information Age, Artech House, 1999. ISBN 978-0-89006-526-0.
  2. F. Neri, Introduction to Electronic Defense Systems, 2nd ed., SciTech, 2006.
  3. R. Price, "A Useful Theorem for Nonlinear Devices Having Gaussian Inputs," IRE Trans. Information Theory, 4(2), 69–72, 1958.

docs.title: Tracking and estimation
docs.text:
1. Y. Bar-Shalom, X. R. Li and T. Kirubarajan, Estimation with Applications to Tracking and Navigation, Wiley, 2001. ISBN 978-0-471-41655-5.
  2. S. S. Blackman, Multiple-Target Tracking with Radar Applications, Artech House, 1986.
  3. H. W. Kuhn, "The Hungarian Method for the Assignment Problem," Naval Research Logistics Quarterly, 2, 83–97, 1955.
  4. S. M. Sherman and D. K. Barton, Monopulse Principles and Techniques, 2nd ed., Artech House, 2011.

docs.title: Imaging
docs.text:
1. I. G. Cumming and F. H. Wong, Digital Processing of Synthetic Aperture Radar Data, Artech House, 2005.
  2. C. C. Chen and H. C. Andrews, "Target-Motion-Induced Radar Imaging," IEEE Trans. AES, 16(1), 2–14, 1980.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text:
1. IEEE Std 686-2017, IEEE Standard for Radar Definitions.
  2. NATO APP-6, Joint Military Symbology (affiliation shapes and colours on the scopes).

docs.title: Writing scenarios
docs.text:
A scenario is a YAML (or JSON) file with up to six sections. Everything is optional except a radar and at least the targets you want; anything left out takes the default in the tables below. Unknown keys are not silently dropped: the loader lists them as warnings, with a suggestion when the key looks like a typo (rain_rate_mmhr → rain_rate_mm_hr).

Coordinates are East-North-Up in metres with the origin anywhere you like (usually the radar). Azimuths are degrees clockwise from North. See Conventions.

A minimal file:

scenario:
  name: "Two aircraft"
radar:
  frequency_hz: 3.0e9
  power_watts: 200000
  antenna: {gain_db: 35, beamwidth_az_deg: 1.5, scan_rate_rpm: 12}
targets:
  - name: "Inbound"
    affiliation: hostile
    rcs_m2: 5
    initial_position: {x_m: 20000, y_m: 60000, z_m: 4000}
    velocity: {vx_mps: -100, vy_mps: -250, vz_mps: 0}

The fastest way to start a new one is the scenario editor, which writes this format.

docs.title: scenario
docs.text: Key Default Meaning name Unnamed Scenario shown in the header description one or two sentences duration_seconds 180 used by the command-line runner update_rate_hz 30 engine steps per simulated second seed none random seed (also accepted under simulation)

docs.text:
A list; each entry:

Key Default Meaning name Target_n type aircraft free text (fighter, missile, ship, …) affiliation unknown friend, hostile, neutral, unknown (display only) rcs_m2 1 mean RCS swerling_model 1 0–4 initial_position origin {x_m, y_m, z_m}, z = altitude velocity 0 {vx_mps, vy_mps, vz_mps} acceleration 0 {ax_mps2, ay_mps2, az_mps2}: constant acceleration turn_rate_deg_s 0 constant-rate turn, positive = right deploy_time_s 0 appears at this time has_ecm false carries a jammer ecm_type noise_barrage noise_barrage, noise_spot, drfm ecm_power_watts 1000 jammer ERP ecm_bandwidth_hz 100e6 noise bandwidth drfm {mode: rgpo|vgpo, gain_over_skin_db, capture_dwell_s, pull_rate_mps, max_pull_m, vgpo_rate_hz_per_s, max_doppler_pull_hz, inherent_delay_s}

docs.title: ecm
docs.text:
Expendables released during the run. With deployed_by they start at that target's position at deploy_time_s; otherwise give a position.

ecm:
  decoys:
    - name: "MALD"
      deployed_by: "F-16 Alpha"
      deploy_time_s: 30
      velocity: {vx_mps: 300, vy_mps: 30, vz_mps: -5}
      rcs_m2: 5
  chaff_clouds:
    - name: "Chaff 1"
      deployed_by: "F-16 Alpha"
      deploy_time_s: 60
      rcs_m2: 50          # fully bloomed
      bloom_time_s: 1     # rise time constant
      decay_time_s: 120   # dispersal time constant

A decoy without its own velocity keeps the carrier's velocity; chaff without one falls at 1 m/s.

docs.title: Built-in scenarios
docs.text:
Each scenario is a small YAML or JSON file under radarsim/scenarios/. They are written to show one effect clearly, and the test suite checks that each one still does what is described here (tests/test_scenarios.py).

Run any of them from File › Built-in scenarios, or without the interface with radarsim --headless <name>.

docs.title: basic_tracking
docs.text: X-band surveillance radar (10 GHz, 200 kW, 12 rpm) and three targets at about 40 km: a 15 m² aircraft, a 5 m² fighter (Swerling 3) and a 0.5 m² cruise missile at 100 m (Swerling 2). All three are detected on every scan and confirmed after three scans. A good place to learn the scopes and the track life cycle.

docs.title: close_air_combat
docs.text: A fighter AESA rasters ±60° about North at 120°/s from 8 km while flying North at 250 m/s. Bandit 1 breaks right at 9°/s (about 4.7 g) and carries a DRFM; Bandit 2 drifts out of the sector to the West behind a spot-noise jammer. Shows sector scanning in the B-scope, a single unbroken track through a hard turn (the scenario sets the tracker's process noise to 40 m/s²) and a target that is lost because it leaves the scan volume rather than because of detection.

docs.title: drone_swarm_saturation
docs.text: Thirty 0.01 m² drones in three ranks approach a C-band radar. Single-look SNR is around 20 dB at 15 km, so most looks detect, but the drones are close together and the tracker initiates and drops tracks as associations swap. Useful for looking at data-association limits.

docs.title: ecm_environment
docs.text: Low-power X-band radar over sea state 2 with a 500 W barrage jammer on a bomber and a DRFM on a fighter. The bomber stays hidden (jamming costs about 35 dB), the fighter is detected intermittently.

docs.title: f16_vs_sa6
docs.text: S-band search radar (500 kW, 100 MHz pulse compression, CA-CFAR) against two F-16s coming in from the West. Alpha runs a 200 W barrage jammer and is never detected; it releases an ADM-160 MALD at 30 s and a chaff cloud at 60 s, both from its own position. The decoy and the chaff are detected and tracked within one scan of their release, while Bravo is tracked from about 73 km.

docs.title: ground_clutter_filtering
docs.text: L-band radar on a 30 m tower over land with urban, rural and forest clutter sectors. Two low flyers sit in clutter; a two-pulse MTI and a 24-cell GO-CFAR bring them out (SCR around 30 dB with MTI). Switch MTI canceller off in the settings to watch the clutter loss jump and the low flyers drop out.

docs.title: hypersonic_interception
docs.text: A Ka-band seeker at 20 km altitude stares East at a glide vehicle closing at about 3 km/s. The seeker first detects it at roughly 14 s. The radial speed is far beyond the unambiguous Doppler of the 100 kHz PRF, which the range–Doppler view shows when pulse-Doppler processing is switched on.

docs.title: mountain_ambush
docs.text: A ground radar 30 m above the terrain, a 2.5–3 km ridge to the North-East (procedural relief plus three Gaussian peaks), and a low flyer running West behind it at 1500 m. The flyer is masked until it clears the northern end of the ridge at about 2½ minutes; MTI then lifts it out of the mountain clutter. A high-altitude aircraft to the East is visible throughout.

docs.title: naval_battlegroup
docs.text: S-band naval radar on a 35 m mast, NRL sea clutter at sea state 4, a carrier at 80 km and four sea-skimming missiles (0.1–0.15 m², 5–8 m above the water). Pulse compression (10 µs, 10 MHz) and MTI keep the clutter loss to a few dB, and all four missiles are detected on the first scan. Switch MTI off to see sea clutter take over.

docs.title: stealth_deep_penetration
docs.text:
UHF early-warning radar (450 MHz, 400 kW, 200 µs pulse) and a 0.01 m² bomber starting 250 km out. RadarSim's RCS does not depend on frequency, so the value in the file should be the one that applies at the radar frequency; with this value the bomber is first detected near the end of the five-minute run.

Limitations worth knowing

The detection model assumes the target sits in an unambiguous range cell; range ambiguities of high-PRF waveforms appear only in the pulse-Doppler processor. RCS is aspect dependent (broadside-weighted) but frequency independent.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
RadarSim's test suite has 421 tests. They run on every push for Python 3.9 to 3.12 on Linux, and on Windows and macOS. Most of them compare a model with an independent result rather than with its own earlier output.

pip install -e ".[gui,dev]"
pytest                              # about 40 s

docs.title: What is checked
docs.text:
Area Reference used by the tests Radar equation Skolnik 2008, example 2.1: SNR 17.26 dB to within 0.01 dB Detection range free-space range grows as σ^¼ to within 2 % Swerling Pd, cases 0–4 pulse-level Monte Carlo of a square-law detector, 200 000 looks, 1 and 8 pulses Albersheim inverse consistency with the exact Pd CFAR multipliers (CA, GO, SO, OS) measured false-alarm rate on exponential noise CFAR loss ordering SO > OS > GO > CA and known CA values ITU-R P.676-13 ITU validation workbook, 12 significant digits ITU-R P.838-3 published coefficients Sea clutter NRL model reference values Doppler \(f_d = -2v_r/\lambda\), sign and magnitude Pulse-Doppler chain matched-filter gain τB, peak in the right range and velocity bin, MTI null at DC Antenna pattern half power at half the 3 dB beamwidth Kinematics constant velocity, constant acceleration, exact coordinated turn on a circle Terrain mountain peaks block the ray, flat terrain does not Tracking straight-line convergence, NIS consistency, confirmation through a 4.7 g turn without a break Jamming J/S scaling with range and bandwidth, burn-through consistency Receiver limiter complex-Gaussian closed form at full scale Determinism same seed gives identical runs; reset reproduces a run exactly Scenarios every shipped scenario has no unknown keys, survives export and reload unchanged, and does what its description says (tests/test_scenarios.py) Interface every scenario loads with its radar values intact, every scope renders, settings reach the engine, editor round trip, recording and replay, a bad file leaves the run going

tests/test_known_defects.py keeps one test for each defect fixed during the 4.0 overhaul, so none of them can come back unnoticed.

docs.title: Monte Carlo against theory
docs.text: The coverage curve of the basic_tracking radar for a 1 m² target, with empirical detection rates from 400 independent looks per range and their 95 % Wilson intervals:

docs.title: Signal-level output
docs.text: A range–Doppler map from the coherent processor: three targets, LFM pulse compression, Hamming-windowed 64-point Doppler FFT. Closing targets appear at negative radial velocity.

docs.title: Reproducing the figures
docs.text:
python tools/make_figures.py          # docs/assets/figures
python tools/capture_screenshots.py   # docs/assets/screens

docs.title: Clutter and MTI
docs.text: Code: radarsim/physics/clutter.py, radarsim/simulation/engine.py.

docs.title: Surface reflectivity
docs.text:
Surface Model Domain land (rural, urban, forest, …) constant-γ: \(\sigma^0 = \gamma \sin\psi\), γ from a short table or a measured value any grazing angle bare soil (ground_surface.model: oh1992) Oh, Sarabandi & Ulaby (1992) empirical model 1–10 GHz, 10–70° incidence, \(0.1 \le ks \le 6\) sea NRL five-parameter model (Gregers-Hansen & Mital 2012), HH and VV 0.5–35 GHz, sea state 0–6, 0.1–60° grazing

Outside the Oh-1992 incidence range (a ground radar looking at a distant target sees grazing angles of a fraction of a degree) the engine falls back to constant-γ instead of extrapolating. Polarisation tilt mixes the HH and VV values. Clutter sectors in a scenario change the surface class and add a calibration offset for regions of azimuth and range.

docs.title: Clutter in the target's cell
docs.text:
The surface patch sharing the target's range cell has area

\[ A_c \approx \frac{\pi}{4}\, \min\!\left(\frac{c\tau_c}{2\cos\psi},\, \frac{2R\tan(\theta_{el}/2)}{\sin\psi}\right) \cdot 2R\tan\!\left(\frac{\theta_{az}}{2}\right) \]

with the compressed pulse length \(\tau_c\). The beam is pointed at the target, so the patch, at depression angle \(-\psi\), is seen through the elevation pattern \(g(\Delta) = \max\{e^{-4\ln 2\,\Delta^2/\theta_{el}^2},\,10^{SLL/10}\}\) at \(\Delta = \epsilon_t + \psi\), twice (transmit and receive):

\[ \sigma_c = \sigma^0 A_c\, g(\Delta)^2 . \]

A low flyer competes with the full main-beam clutter; an aircraft several beamwidths up sees it only through the sidelobes. The test suite checks that a target at 6 km altitude loses at least 10 dB less to clutter than one at 50 m at the same range.

docs.title: MTI
docs.text:
A two-pulse canceller removes returns near zero Doppler. Its improvement factor against clutter with a Gaussian spectrum of width \(\sigma_c = 2\sigma_v/\lambda\) (Skolnik 2008, eqs. 2.41–2.42) is

\[ I_1 = 2\left(\frac{f_r}{2\pi\sigma_c}\right)^2, \qquad I = \left(\frac{1}{I_1} + \frac{1}{I_{s}}\right)^{-1}, \]

limited by the system stability \(I_s\) = 50 dB. The clutter velocity spread defaults to 0.25 m/s over land and 1 m/s over sea (Nathanson 1999) and can be set per scenario. Targets whose radial speed is below the MTI threshold are cancelled with the clutter.

docs.title: Validity
docs.text:
• Clutter is treated as noise-like in the SINR (no Weibull/K-distribution tails in the detection decision); the distributions are available as samplers in ClutterModel for signal-level work.
  • One clutter patch per target cell; range-ambiguous clutter from earlier pulses is not added.

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: Code: radarsim/simulation/engine.py (SimulationEngine.step), radarsim/physics/radar_equation.py, radarsim/physics/metrics.py.

docs.title: When a target is looked at
docs.text:
A rotating antenna only illuminates a target while its beam passes over it. RadarSim records, for every engine step, the azimuth interval the beam centre swept (Radar.swept_legs) and gives a target exactly one detection opportunity, a look, in the step in which the beam centre crosses its azimuth. A circular scan therefore looks at each target once per revolution, a sector raster twice per cycle, and a staring antenna on every step while the target is in the main lobe.

The pulses that hit the target during the dwell are represented by the non-coherent integration count pulses_integrated.

Between looks the full physics chain is not evaluated; the last look's SNR and Pd are carried forward with updated geometry. With 30 targets this keeps a step near 1 ms.

docs.title: SNR of one look
docs.text:
Receiver-input SNR from the monostatic radar equation (Skolnik 2008, eq. 2.6):

\[ \mathrm{SNR}_{in} = \frac{P_t G^2 \lambda^2 \bar\sigma}{(4\pi)^3 R^4 \, k T_0 F B \, L_s L_a} \]

with \(\bar\sigma\) the aspect-weighted mean RCS, \(L_s\) the system losses and \(L_a\) the two-way propagation loss. The matched filter adds the time-bandwidth gain \(G_c = \max(1, \tau B)\) for the signal only. Noise, noise jamming and clutter are combined after the matched filter as inverse SNR terms (Richards 2005, §2.4, §4.6):

\[ \mathrm{SINR} = \left( \frac{1}{G_c\,\mathrm{SNR}_{in}} + \frac{J/S}{G_c} + \frac{\sigma_c}{\bar\sigma} \right)^{-1} \]

Thermal noise and barrage jamming are white over the receiver band and gain nothing from compression; clutter is an echo of the same waveform, so it is compressed like the target, and its resolution cell uses the compressed pulse length \(\tau_c = \min(\tau, 1/B)\). The receiver hard limiter is applied to the receiver-input powers, and any clipping loss is subtracted at the end.

docs.title: Probability of detection
docs.text:
The Swerling fluctuation is not sampled: SNR uses the mean RCS and Pd averages over the fluctuation statistics, which is what Swerling's results describe. The threshold of the square-law detector integrating \(N\) pulses is set from the false-alarm probability, \(P_{fa} = Q(N, T)\), and

Case Pd 0 non-central χ² survival, \(\Pr\{\chi'^2_{2N}(2N\,\mathrm{SNR}) > 2T\}\) 1, 3 the Swerling 0 result averaged over an exponential (1) or χ²₄ (3) RCS, constant over the dwell 2, 4 the same averaged over the sum of \(N\) independent per-pulse RCS values

Cases 1 and 2 use their exact closed forms (DiFranco & Rubin 1968); for case 2 the integrated statistic is simply \((1+\mathrm{SNR})\,\Gamma(N)\). Cases 3 and 4 are averaged numerically over the RCS distribution with Gauss–Legendre rules split at the detection knee, accurate to about \(10^{-5}\) (radarsim.physics.metrics.calculate_pd_swerling). All five are checked against a pulse-level Monte Carlo in the test suite.

docs.title: CFAR loss
docs.text:
An adaptive threshold estimated from \(N\) reference cells needs more SNR than a detector that knows the noise level. RadarSim computes this CFAR loss for CA, GO, SO and OS (rank \(3N/4\)) detectors from the exact single-pulse Swerling-1 expressions (Gandhi & Kassam 1988; Rohling 1983) at \(P_d = 0.5\) and subtracts it from every look's SINR before Pd is evaluated.

N CA GO SO OS 16 2.00 dB 2.21 dB 3.76 dB 2.90 dB 24 1.30 dB 1.48 dB 2.33 dB 1.92 dB 32 0.97 dB 1.12 dB 1.67 dB 1.44 dB

(Pfa = 10⁻⁶.)

docs.title: Measurements
docs.text: A detected look produces a range and two angles with Gaussian errors (range_noise_std_m, angle_noise_std_rad) or, with monopulse enabled, angles from the sum/difference estimator (Tracking). The measured position, converted to the ground plane, goes to the tracker.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: Coverage in the analysis drawer evaluates this chain for a probe target over range. Free-space detection range at fixed SNR grows as \(\sigma^{1/4}\); the test suite checks this to 2 %.

docs.title: Electronic attack
docs.text:
Code: radarsim/physics/ecm.py, radarsim/simulation/engine.py.

Every jammer-equipped target uses its own technique from the scenario (ecm_type). The Jammers on switch turns all of them on or off, and Technique can force one technique on every jammer to compare them.

docs.title: Noise jamming
docs.text:
For a self-screening jammer of ERP \(P_j G_j\) and bandwidth \(B_j\) against a radar of bandwidth \(B_r\) (Schleher 1999, §4.2):

\[ \frac{J}{S} = \frac{P_j G_j\, 4\pi R^2\, B_r}{P_t G_t \sigma\, B_j}\cdot\frac{L_s}{L_j}, \qquad B_r/B_j \le 1 . \]

The jammer's one-way path suffers half the propagation and system loss of the radar's two-way path. Jamming enters the SINR after the matched filter divided by the compression gain, like thermal noise (Detection). Spot and barrage jammers differ only in bandwidth. With frequency agility on, the jammer has to spread over 10 % of the carrier frequency.

The burn-through range, where \(S/J\) reaches the required SNR, is

\[ R_{bt} = \sqrt{\frac{P_t G_t \sigma\, B_j}{4\pi P_j G_j\, \mathrm{SNR}_{req}\, B_r}} . \]

The self-check validate_burn_through_range confirms that calculate_jsr gives exactly \(-\mathrm{SNR}_{req}\) at this range. The event log reports when a jammed target is first detected despite jamming (burn-through).

docs.title: DRFM deception
docs.text: A digital RF memory captures the radar pulse and plays it back, delayed (range gate pull-off, RGPO) or Doppler-shifted (velocity gate pull-off, VGPO), with a gain over the skin return. The jammer state machine (idle → capture → pull → reset) uses the dwell, pull rate and maximum pull from the scenario. The false return appears as a ghost target moving away from the real one along the line of sight; in the pulse-Doppler processor it is injected phase-coherently into the CPI.

docs.title: Chaff and decoys
docs.text:
Chaff clouds and decoys are radar objects in their own right, released at a given time, optionally from a named aircraft's position. Chaff has a large, Swerling 2 cross-section (many independently moving dipoles) that blooms and then decays,

\[ \sigma(t) = \sigma_{max}\,(1 - e^{-t/\tau_b})\,e^{-t/\tau_d}, \]

and falls slowly. A decoy flies its own course with its own RCS. Both are detected and tracked exactly like aircraft, which is the point: the radar cannot tell them apart by detection alone.

docs.title: Validity
docs.text:
• No jammer antenna pattern or sidelobe jamming geometry beyond the self-screening case; stand-off jammers are not modelled.
  • Noise jamming is treated as white Gaussian noise in the receiver band.

docs.title: Propagation and terrain
docs.text: Code: radarsim/physics/atmospheric.py, rain.py, terrain.py.

docs.title: Gaseous absorption
docs.text:
Specific attenuation of oxygen and water vapour follows the line-by-line method of ITU-R P.676-13 Annex 1 (44 oxygen and 35 water-vapour lines plus the dry continuum), valid from 1 to 1000 GHz. The test suite reproduces the ITU validation workbook to 12 significant digits. The Recommendation is written in terms of the dry-air pressure \(p\); scenarios give the barometric pressure, and the engine passes \(p = P - e\) with the water-vapour pressure \(e = \rho T / 216.7\).

The path loss is \(2\gamma R\) for the two-way path. Below 1 GHz gaseous absorption is negligible and is set to zero.

docs.title: Rain
docs.text:
Specific attenuation \(\gamma_R = k R^{\alpha}\) uses the ITU-R P.838-3 coefficients for the radar's frequency and polarisation tilt. Rain only fills the layer below the rain height \(h_R = h_0 + 0.36\) km (ITU-R P.839-4, \(h_0 = 3\) km by default), so the attenuated length is the part of the slant path below \(h_R\). A target above the rain layer sees less attenuation and no rain clutter in its own cell.

Rain also returns power: the volume reflectivity from the Marshall–Palmer Z–R relation, \(Z = 200 R^{1.6}\), \(\eta = \pi^5 |K|^2 Z / \lambda^4\), times a resolution cell of \((\pi/4) R^2 \theta_{az}\theta_{el}\,c\tau_c/2\).

docs.title: Terrain and line of sight
docs.text:
Terrain height is procedural fractal noise (octaves, persistence and lacunarity are configurable) plus optional Gaussian peaks of 10 km standard deviation. The same function feeds the RHI profile, the 3D view and the line-of-sight test.

Line of sight marches along the straight ray from radar to target. Heights in a scenario are altitudes above the curved surface, so at ground distance \(d_1\) from the radar and \(d_2\) from the target the ray must clear

\[ h_{terrain}(x, y) + \frac{d_1 d_2}{2 k R_E}, \qquad k = 4/3, \]

the Earth bulge of the 4/3-radius model (Skolnik 2008, §2.12). A masked target gets no SNR and cannot be detected; the event log records when it becomes masked and when it reappears.

docs.title: Validity
docs.text:
• Propagation is straight-line with the standard 4/3 Earth; ducting and multipath lobing are not modelled.
  • P.676 is used along a horizontal path at the given pressure and temperature; slant paths through the atmosphere are not integrated layer by layer.

docs.title: Tracking
docs.text:
Code: radarsim/tracking/tracker.py, kalman.py, ekf.py, monopulse.py.

The engine feeds every detection, converted from measured range, azimuth and elevation to a position on the ground plane, to a track-while-scan tracker.

docs.title: Filter
docs.text:
Each track is a constant-velocity Kalman filter on \([x, y, \dot x, \dot y]\) with continuous white-noise acceleration (Bar-Shalom, Li & Kirubarajan 2001, §6.2.2):

\[ Q(\Delta t) = q\begin{bmatrix} \Delta t^3/3 & \Delta t^2/2 \\ \Delta t^2/2 & \Delta t \end{bmatrix} \otimes I_2, \qquad q = \sigma_a^2 \cdot 1\,\mathrm{s}. \]

Unlike the discrete-step variant, the covariance added over a revisit interval does not depend on how many simulation steps it is split into. The default \(\sigma_a\) = 10 m/s² suits transport aircraft; close_air_combat raises it to 40 m/s² to hold a 4.7 g turn. An extended Kalman filter with polar measurements and SNR-dependent noise is available through TrackManager.set_ekf_mode.

docs.title: Association
docs.text: Detections are assigned to tracks by global nearest neighbour (Hungarian algorithm) with a χ² gate at 99.73 % on the normalised innovation squared. A track with only one detection has no velocity yet, so it uses a velocity gate instead, \(|z_2 - z_1| \le v_{max}\,\Delta t + 3\sqrt{2}\,\sigma_z\), and on the second hit is initialised by two-point differencing (velocity from the two positions, covariance from the measurement noise).

docs.title: Life cycle
docs.text:
• tentative after the first detection; dropped after two misses;
  • confirmed after three consecutive hits (configurable);
  • coasting after a miss, back to confirmed on the next hit;
  • lost after three misses, or when it has not been updated for 3.5 revisit periods (a target that left a sector scan for good).

A miss is only charged when the beam actually looked at the track's predicted position in that step and the track has not already been updated during the current scan, so tracks between beam passes simply coast.

docs.title: Monopulse
docs.text:
With Monopulse on, angles come from an amplitude-comparison estimator instead of fixed angle noise. Two Gaussian beams squinted by \(\pm\theta_s\) give

\[ \varepsilon(\theta) = \frac{\Delta}{\Sigma} = \tanh\!\left(\frac{4\ln 2\,\theta\,\theta_s}{\theta_3^2}\right), \qquad k_m = \frac{4\ln 2\,\theta_s}{\theta_3}, \]

linear near boresight and saturating off axis. Thermal noise gives the accuracy \(\sigma_\theta = \theta_3 / (k_m\sqrt{2\,\mathrm{SNR}})\) (Barton 2005), applied to \(\varepsilon\) before inversion.

docs.title: Validity
